lines.content: This repository is a starter template for a greenfield Java project used in an introductory software engineering course in an undergraduate computer science program. Students use it as the starting point for their own projects.

Unless the user says otherwise, assume that you are assisting a student working on a project in this repository. If the user identifies themselves as an instructor or another project stakeholder, adapt your response to that role.
* Prior knowledge: Basic Java and OOP concepts.
* Level of programming experience: [to be filled]
* IDE and level of expertise: [to be filled]
* Explain the rationale for significant actions: what you did and why.
* Keep explanations brief but instructive, supporting learning through responsible use of AI. For example:
* When suggesting a Git command, briefly explain what it does.
* Add explanatory Javadoc comments to all classes and to nontrivial methods and fields when their purpose or behavior is not obvious.
* Make generated code as self-explanatory as possible, and include explanatory comments where they improve understanding.
* When faced with a design choice, choose the simplest option that is sufficient for the requirements, while briefly explaining relevant more advanced alternatives.
Ensure that Java 25 is used when running the application or build tasks. On macOS, use `sdk use java 25.0.3.fx-zulu` to switch to Java 25 if needed.
Follow the [SE-EDU Java Coding Standard](https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html) (intermediate level) for all code in this project.
For other topics not covered, refer to the [Google Java Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html).
Use lightweight tags unless the user requests an annotated tag.
When proposing or creating a commit message, include enough detail to explain the rationale for the change.
Do not commit or push unless explicitly asked.
Reasonable use of OOP, e.g., at least some use of inheritance, with code divided into classes in a sensible way (e.g., Ui, Storage, Parser, Todo, Deadline, Event, etc.).
At least half of the public methods/classes have Javadoc comments.
- No blatant violations of the coding standard (both Java and Git conventions).
- The code is neat, e.g., no chunks of commented-out code.
- At least some errors are handled using exceptions.
Submitted some deliverables in at least 4 out of the 6 iP weeks (i.e., week 2 to week 7)
Followed the other specified requirements (e.g., using Git/GitHub for each increment and doing peer reviews) in at least 4 weeks
The product website and the user guide:
- Provide enough guidance to the user. Cover all non-trivial features.
- No major formatting errors in the published view.
This is a project template for a greenfield Java project. Given below are instructions on how to use it.
Prerequisites: JDK 25, update Intellij to the most recent version.
1. Open Intellij (if you are not in the welcome screen, click `File` > `Close Project` to close the existing project first)
1. Open the project into Intellij as follows:
1. Select the project directory, and click `OK`.
1. If there are any further prompts, accept the defaults.
1. Configure the project to use **JDK 25** (not other versions) as explained in [here](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/sdk.html#set-up-jdk).
In the same dialog, set the **Project language level** field to the `SDK default` option.

1. After that, locate the `src/main/java/Chre.java` file, right-click it, and choose `Run Chre.main()` (if the code editor is showing compile errors, try restarting the IDE). If the setup is correct, you should see something like the below as the output:

**Warning:** Keep the `src\main\java` folder as the root folder for Java files (i.e., don't rename those folders or move Java files to another folder outside of this folder path), as this is the default location some tools (e.g., Gradle) expect to find Java files.
// Describe the action and its outcome.
// A description of the expected outcome goes here
* Chre is a simple chatbot that manages tasks.
* Orchestrates the Ui, Parser, and TaskList components.
* Main entry point for the Chre chatbot application.
* Coordinates user input, task management, and output.
* Parser interprets user input and identifies commands.
* Parses the user input and returns the command type.
* Extracts the first word as the command.
* Extracts the task index from a mark/unmark command.
* @return the task index as a string, or empty if no index found
* Extracts the task description from an "add" command.
* For "add Buy groceries" or just "Buy groceries", returns the task text.
* Task represents a single task with a description and completion status.
* Constructs a Task with the given name.
* Returns whether this task is done.
* Marks this task as done or not done.
* @param done true to mark as done, false to mark as not done
* Returns the task with its completion status.
* Format: [X] name (if done) or [ ] name (if not done)
* @return the task string with status indicator
* TaskList manages a collection of Task tasks.
* Provides methods to add tasks and retrieve the complete list.
* Adds a new task to the list.
* @param description the task description to add
* Returns all tasks in the list.
* Marks a task as done by its 1-based index.
* @param index the 1-based index of the task to mark as done
* Marks a task as not done by its 1-based index.
* @param index the 1-based index of the task to unmark
* Returns the number of tasks in the list.
* Ui handles all user interface interactions.
* Manages input reading and output display.
* Constructs a Ui object and initializes the scanner and display elements.
* Displays the welcome message and banner.
System.out.println("What can I do for you?");
System.out.println("Bye. Hope to see you again soon!");
* Reads a command from the user.
* Displays all tasks in the list with 1-based numbering.
* @param tasks the list of tasks to display
* Displays a confirmation message when a task is added.
* @param task the task that was added
* Displays a confirmation message when a task is marked as done.
* @param task the task that was marked as done
System.out.println("Nice! I've marked this task as done:");
* Displays a confirmation message when a task is unmarked.
* @param task the task that was unmarked
System.out.println("OK, I've marked this task as not done yet:");
